title: Ciauscolo Spalmabile
author: Marco Bellini
desc: The Marche's uniquely spreadable cured salami, finely ground pork smoked gently and cured until soft enough to spread directly onto warm, toasted bread like a rich pate.
longDesc: Unlike most Italian salami, which are meant to be thinly sliced, ciauscolo is deliberately ground extremely fine and cured to a genuinely soft, spreadable consistency, a texture that sets it apart from virtually every other cured meat in Italian charcuterie.
ingredients: 200 g (7 oz) ciauscolo (or substitute a soft, spreadable Italian salami)
steps: Bring the ciauscolo to room temperature, which makes it easier to spread.
Toast slices of crusty bread lightly.
Spread the ciauscolo generously over the warm toasted bread, similar to a pate.
Add a light drizzle of honey if desired, for a sweet contrast.
Garnish with a little fresh rosemary and serve immediately.
chefTips: Bringing the ciauscolo to room temperature is essential for easy, even spreading.
Warm, freshly toasted bread makes for the most pleasant contrast against the soft, rich meat.
A light drizzle of honey is a traditional, welcome addition that balances the meat richness.
commonMistakes: Serving straight from the refrigerator, when it is too firm to spread easily.
Overloading the bread, when a moderate, even layer is more traditional and enjoyable.
Substituting a firm, slice-only salami, which will not replicate the intended spreadable texture.
servedWith: A glass of red wine from the Marche
storage: Refrigerate for up to 1 week once opened.
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein, best enjoyed in moderation given its cured, rich nature.
culturalNote: Ciauscolo holds a protected geographic status in the Marche and Umbria, its uniquely spreadable texture setting it apart from virtually all other Italian cured meats.
